steps.what: Select treatment, therapy, medication or preventive care with the patient
Prescribe selected care and assess medication surveillance alerts
Administer indicated treatment or vaccination and observe the patient's response

tasks.design: Keep treatment selection, prescription authorisation and physical care with the physician. Existing rule-based medication surveillance in {OTHER}, the clinical prescribing system, remains in use without a new model or additional automation claim.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appropriate treatment depends on clinical context and patient preferences.
tasks.enabler_now: Medication surveillance already supports prescribing, but its runtime is not new labour savings.
tasks.still_hard: An alert needs interpretation and a treatment still requires patient agreement and safe delivery.
tasks.human_edge: Balance benefit, risk and the patient's goals and take responsibility for care.
tasks.altitude: Treatment responsibilities and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: G-Standaard supports interaction, contraindication, dose and duplicate medication checks; these do not replace prescription authorisation.

assumptions: Boundary is this physician's treatment selection, prescribing and hands-on care; delegated nursing administration is outside the denominator.

The physician verifies current medication, allergies and selected dose within s2. Existing record producers and surveillance remain under present arrangements, with no new structured input or capture duty.
Existing native surveillance is retained without modification; no new deployment or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Current prescribing system and clinical responsibilities
research_questions: Which medication alerts require pharmacist discussion under current procedures?

already_counted.description: Treatment choice, prescription authorisation and administration

incremental.description: No added system or workflow maintenance

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, treatment, medication, dose, route, timing and reviewed alerts; changes void authorisation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Existing medication-check runtime and physical care yield no new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order and interpret tests to diagnose patients

steps.what: Select and order tests based on the clinical question
Perform relevant clinical tests and establish reliable findings
Interpret tests, records and examination information to diagnose the condition
outputs: clinical diagnosis or further diagnostic plan

tasks.design: Retain test selection, hands-on testing and diagnostic interpretation with the physician using {OTHER}, the clinical record and ordering system. No general diagnostic model or automated test-order decision is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The significance of a test result depends on the clinical question and the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing results and order screens already support the retained decision process.
tasks.still_hard: Normal results may not explain symptoms and abnormal results may be incidental.
tasks.human_edge: Integrate evidence, uncertainty and the patient's story into a defensible diagnosis.
tasks.altitude: Diagnostic responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: The digest's specialised imaging examples do not establish general family-medicine diagnosis automation; no saving is assumed here.

assumptions: Boundary includes this physician's ordering, personally performed tests and interpretation. External diagnostic service performance and report production remain outside the denominator.
Existing diagnostic services produce returned reports through the current workflow; no new structured input or interface is required.
Existing native result views remain unchanged. No deployment or incremental upkeep is added, justifying zero.
unknowns: Personally performed test mix and current result interfaces
research_questions: Which diagnostic uncertainties require specialist interpretation?

already_counted.description: Test selection, personal testing and diagnostic interpretation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. No clinical judgement or physical testing is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Collect patient history and examination findings during the consultation
Record history, findings and relevant reports in a patient note

loop.purpose: Draft a clinical note from the consultation and clinician-supplied findings
loop.input: Permitted consultation capture, dictated observations and selected existing reports
loop.output: Draft note distinguishing reported history, observed findings and agreed plan
loop.check: Physician compares draft meaning with the consultation, checks negation, attribution, medication details and omitted relevant findings
loop.stop: One correction cycle then manual note entry if source capture or meaning is unreliable
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates support structure but narrative history and findings require semantic drafting

steps.what: Verify the note and maintain the authoritative patient record

tasks.design: Test native templates and dictation in {OTHER}, the clinical record system, then use a bounded consultation-note draft if narrative entry remains slow. The physician verifies meaning and final content before filing; patient discussion and examination time remain intact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Turning consultation information into a clear record requires repeated typing and restructuring.
tasks.enabler_now: Consultation scribes can draft notes for clinician validation and supported clinical-record integration.
tasks.still_hard: Negation, uncertain diagnoses and clinically important omissions need careful verification.
tasks.human_edge: Know what was actually established and what remains uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less first-draft note entry; record responsibility and consultation time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Improve note structure and safe record integration
reach.learn: Source attribution, access controls and correction history

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts consultation notes for clinician validation with supported clinical-record integration.
The Capio study reports self-estimated note time falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes with median editing of 93 seconds; this does not establish the saving for this task mix.

assumptions: Boundary is history and findings collection plus patient-note creation and maintenance, excluding diagnostic and treatment decisions assigned to other tasks.

The physician produces history and findings through the full 40-hour consultation step and explicit dictation in retained s2 time. Patient identity, encounter ID, source report IDs and note destination are selected and checked within the 20 retained s2 hours and s3.

Capture permission, microphone operation, dictated nonverbal findings and correction are counted in retained s2 time. If capture is unavailable or unreliable, manual note entry resumes; no free structured history is assumed.
Test native templates and dictation before a scribe. Final write-back follows s3 approval of the exact note; source audio handling and access require local agreement.
unknowns: Permitted consultation capture and source retention
research_questions: Does a local trial reduce note entry after counting setup, dictation and semantic verification without shortening the consultation?

already_counted.description: Capture setup, dictated findings, draft correction and final verification

incremental.description: Review recurring note errors and maintain note guidance
Maintain access, retention and interface controls

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, encounter and final note text including findings, uncertainty and medication details; changes require renewed validation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+20+20=80; gross 20%, minus four focal upkeep gives 16% central net. Low assumes seven drafting hours removed when capture and corrections are harder; collection and final verification remain full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor patient progress and reevaluate treatment

steps.what: Monitor patients' conditions through follow-up history and examination
Reevaluate treatments with the patient and agree any necessary changes

tasks.design: Keep follow-up assessment and treatment reevaluation with the physician and patient. Existing records in {OTHER}, the clinical record system, support the discussion without a new monitoring or recommendation tool.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress depends on symptoms, function, adherence and patient priorities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records already support clinician-led follow-up.
tasks.still_hard: Improvement in one measure may conceal another problem or an unacceptable adverse effect.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret the patient's lived response and agree proportionate next steps.
tasks.altitude: Follow-up responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Clinical follow-up and treatment reevaluation retain their labour; documentation savings are assigned solely to task 7774.

assumptions: Boundary is clinical follow-up and plan reevaluation, excluding record drafting, test performance and prescription issuance counted in their own tasks.
No new structured progress score or remote monitoring capture is required.
Existing native record access is sufficient. No new system or incremental upkeep is added, so ongoing new work is zero.
unknowns: Current follow-up responsibilities and patient needs
research_questions: Which changes in condition require earlier direct review?

already_counted.description: Clinical progress assessment and treatment discussion

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross saving and zero upkeep. Clinical monitoring and treatment reevaluation remain full.

reach: Work with clinical information specialists on safe note integration
